text_blocks.snippet: Doctors diagnose type 2 diabetes using specific blood tests recommended by the American Diabetes Association.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests recommended by the American Diabetes Association

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past three months. A result of 6.5% or higher on two separate tests means you have diabetes. No fasting is required.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least eight hours. A level of 126 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar two hours after you drink a sweet sugary liquid. A level of 200 mg/dL or higher confirms diabetes.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Checks your blood sugar at any time of day when you have severe symptoms of high blood sugar. A level of 200 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes.
Repeat Testing: Doctors usually repeat an abnormal test on a second day to confirm the diagnosis, unless you have very high blood glucose or classic symptoms.
Common Symptoms: These include extreme thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, and constant fatigue.
